summary: Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich and Göttingen, earning his PhD under Franz Kielhorn. He held positions at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, and Kiel, and served as professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1935).

Heinrich Rickert was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Strasbourg. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (~1916–1932).
Heinrich Rückert was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1845–1852) and the University of Breslau (~1852–1875).
Heinrich Schliemann was a scholar in history and archaeology. He pursued studies at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock around 1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Zurich under Bernhard Hirzel, Johann Caspar von Orelli, and Hermann Sauppe. He spent his career at Zurich, becoming Ordinarius for Sanskrit and comparative linguistics in 1864.

Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig (~1865–1870) under Hermann Brockhaus. He served as a classical languages teacher at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Jena, Tübingen (PhD), and Leipzig. He studied with Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Friedrich Max Müller, and held a habilitation post at Leipzig in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Strasbourg, Tübingen, and Berlin under scholars including Rudolf von Roth, Siegfried Goldschmidt, Albrecht Weber, and Ernst Windisch, and held chairs at Greifswald and Berlin.

Heinrich von Stietencron was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, SOAS, and Heidelberg, and held a post at Heidelberg before serving as chairholder at the University of Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.

Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz, learning under Ernst Waldschmidt and Erich Frauwallner. After assistant and docent posts, he served as Chair of Indology at Göttingen (1965–2000).

Heinz Mode was a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Berlin and Basel, learning from G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer. He was a professor of Oriental archaeology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1948–1978).

Helen Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, and joined the faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa around 1993.

Helen Hardacre is a scholar of Japanology and religion who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton, Griffith University, and Harvard University, where she was appointed in 1992.
Helen Wang is a scholar of history, archaeology, and numismatics. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1984–1988) and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, as attested in 1999.
Helena Michie is an academic who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Rice University beginning around 1989.

Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich in 1967. She served as an editorial consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1964.
Hellfried Dahlmann was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1935–1941) and the University of Cologne (~1952–1971).

Hellmut Wilhelm was a sinologist who earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke. He taught at Peking University (~1933–1948) and held the chair of sinology at the University of Washington from 1948 to 1971.

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD 1948) and under Paul Debes. He served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1956 to 1988.
